name: Carpenters', Roofers', and Plaisterers' Guild
description: The municipal guild responsible for woodwork, roofing, and the structural integrity of buildings within Waterdeep. They operate primarily out of a headquarters known as the Stone House.
key_facts: Kelso, a heavy-handed guild inspector, attempted to extort the party for 2,000 gold dragons to clear a structural menace violation at the manor.
The party bypassed Kelso by visiting Halthos 'The Hammer' Blund at the Stone House, officially transferring the renovation contract to their neighbor, Tally Fellbranch.
gm_notes: The party made an enemy of Kelso by undercutting his exorbitant quote, but secured a high-quality, magical restoration of their tavern by working the guild's bureaucracy in their favor.

name: Guild of Stonecutters, Masons, Potters, and Tile-makers
description: The strict regulatory body governing stonecraft, foundations, and masonry, operating out of the Builder's Hall in the Southern Ward.
key_facts: Senior Inspector Thorum Slatebreaker issued a fraudulent Notice of Condemnation against Trollskull Manor after accepting a bribe from Emmek Frewn.
The party intimidated Thorum and marched him to the Builder's Hall, exposing his corruption to the honorable Guildmaster Skordar.
Guildmaster Skordar tore up the fraudulent notice, disciplined Thorum, and promised a proper, fee-free inspection.
Master mason Orin Sterling is affiliated with this guild and is capable of performing deep foundation shoring and hydrostatic relief.
gm_notes: Guildmaster Skordar is an honorable dwarf and a potentially powerful ally for Moriah. The party's handling of Thorum cemented their refusal to be bullied by local extortion rackets.

name: Vintners', Distillers', and Brewers' Guild
description: The powerful syndicate that maintains absolute control over the legal sale, distribution, and importation of alcohol in Waterdeep.
key_facts: Mertyn Bottlewick is the guild representative who handles the supply contracts for Trollskull Alley.
To spite their rival Emmek Frewn, the party paid Mertyn a 500 gold piece deposit to become premier partners.
This premium contract grants the manor total exclusivity on rare imports, such as Cormyrean 'Azun's Lament' artwine and 'Iron Heart's Abyss' dwarven cask bourbon from the Spine of the World.
The guild is overseen by Guildmaster Hammond Kraddoc, whose favor is highly sought after by local taverns.
gm_notes: The party heavily invested in this guild to ensure their tavern caters to high-society patrons and dwarven connoisseurs, securing a massive competitive advantage over Frewn's Brews.

name: Dungsweepers', Cellarers', and Plumbers' Guilds
description: The combined municipal forces responsible for sanitation, waste disposal, and subterranean plumbing infrastructure throughout the city's wards.
key_facts: Grubach, a half-orc Dungsweepers' Guild representative, leveraged the threat of 'anonymous health hazard tips' to extort a 20 gold piece per week priority service contract from the party.
Grembo Gribbles, a gnome from the Plumbers' Guild, charged the party 125 gold pieces to permanently seal and sanitize a dangerous, forgotten sewer access point located in the manor's cellar.
gm_notes: Grubach represents the petty, localized corruption the party has to deal with. The urchins and Havik have ongoing plans to recover his ledger and break his extortion racket.

name: Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors
description: The predominant magical guild and auxiliary law enforcement agency for arcane matters in Waterdeep, closely tied to the Blackstaff and Force Grey.
key_facts: Proctor Hex, an agent of the Order, offered the party a 300 gold piece Premier Ward Package to secure Trollskull Manor with permanent Alarm spells and an anti-scrying field.
The Order conducts strict, unannounced arcane audits on commercial properties to ensure licensed spellcasters (like Havik and Cade) are operating safely.
Key figures operating under or alongside the Order include Captain Barnibus Blastwind and Junior Arcanist Velos.
gm_notes: The Order views the party as a high-risk group due to the magical fallout of the fireball incident and their possession of the Stone of Golorr. They demand strict adherence to the city's arcane laws.

name: Fellowship of Innkeepers
description: The fellowship that regulates pricing, quality standards, and zoning for all taverns, inns, and boarding houses in Waterdeep.
key_facts: The guild is represented locally by the charismatic halfling Broxley Fairkettle.

Broxley pushed for a 2,500 gold piece full membership to guarantee guild protection, warning that a 500 gold provisional license would leave the manor vulnerable to price wars and 'random' inspections.
The party negotiated a 'premium independent' exemption to bypass some of the guild's strict standardized pricing structures.
gm_notes: Broxley is friendly but ultimately serves the guild's bottom line. The party relies on pleasing his inspectors to secure a coveted 'Five Tankard' rating.

name: Trollskull Manor Service and Artisan Guilds
description: The myriad of specialized trade guilds that outfitted and certified Trollskull Manor prior to its grand opening.
key_facts: Silas Keen (Glassblowers) installed high-clarity window panes, while Kael Ironhand (Locksmiths) installed dwarf-forged tumbler locks to secure the premises.
Elara Vellum (Scriveners) provided professional branding, calligraphy menus, and municipal filing, while Borb (Coopers) supplied iron-banded oak casks.
Jessa Forgehand (Skilled Smiths) fully outfitted the commercial kitchen with copper-bottomed pots and steel cutlery.
Fendrel Allegro (Musicians) secured a Guild Residency for entertainers, pointedly warning the party that Threestrings was illegally advertising unlicensed performances.

Other essential contractors included Master Willem (Apothecaries) for health certifications, Brenda O'Toole (Carters) for prime delivery routes, Pip & Poppy (Launderers) for linens, Master Foddle (Surveyors) for boundary variances, Tilly Rosebaker (Bakers) for daily bread, and Lena (Lamplighters) for exterior lighting.
gm_notes: This aggregated file ensures the AI knows the specific names of the merchants who provided goods to the tavern, establishing the vast amount of coin the party spent to legitimize their business.
